examples.en: It's dangerous to dig deep into your ear with an ear pick.
Please find the ear pick in the drawer.
Ear picks are made of wood or metal.
I put an ear pick in my travel bag too.
If you don't have an ear pick, use a cotton swab.

examples.ko: 엄마의 귀이개에는 작은 솜털이 달려 있었어요.
examples.en: My mom's ear pick had a small tuft of fluff attached.

explain: '귀이개로 귀를 파다'라는 짝으로 많이 써요. 귀지를 파내는 작은 도구이고, 요즘은 면봉을 더 많이 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: Dad cleaned my ears with an earpick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀이개와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation with 귀이개.
phrases.en_equiv: to clean one's ears with an earpick

phrases.en: It feels refreshing after I dig out the earwax with an earpick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀이개로 무엇을 하는지 구체적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say specifically what you do with an earpick.

phrases.en: You have to be careful when you use an earpick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구를 사용한다는 뜻으로, 주의를 줄 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to use the tool; often used when giving a warning.

explain_en: It is commonly paired as '귀이개로 귀를 파다' (to clean the ear with an ear pick). It's a small tool for removing earwax, though many people now use cotton swabs more.

examples.en: Put the leftover meat in the freezer.

examples.ko: 냉동고가 꽉 차서 더 못 넣어요.
examples.en: The freezer is full, so I can't put in any more.
The freezer door was open and the ice cream melted.
We brought a big new freezer into the shop.
Please take some ice out of the freezer.

examples.ko: 냉동고 속 만두가 벌써 석 달 됐어요.
examples.en: The dumplings in the freezer have been there three months already.

explain: 냉장고 안의 칸은 '냉동실'이라고 하고, 따로 서 있는 큰 냉동 기계나 가게용은 '냉동고'라고 해요. 반대로 차갑지만 얼리지 않는 칸은 '냉장실'이에요.

phrases.en: The ice cream is in the freezer compartment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냉장고 안에 있는 얼리는 칸을 말해요. 집에서는 이 말을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The freezing compartment inside a refrigerator; used more often at home.

phrases.en: Fish keeps a long time if you store it in the freezer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 두려는 음식을 얼려 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when freezing food to keep it for a long time.

phrases.en: The restaurant bought a new commercial freezer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게나 식당에서 쓰는 큰 냉동고를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A large freezer used in shops and restaurants.

explain_en: The compartment inside a refrigerator is called '냉동실', while a separate standing freezer or a shop freezer is '냉동고'. The compartment that is cold but doesn't freeze is '냉장실'.

examples.en: I'm tall, so I hit my head on the doorframe.

examples.ko: 문틀이 휘어서 문이 잘 안 닫혀요.
examples.en: The doorframe is warped, so the door doesn't close well.
I called a company to install a new doorframe.
I wiped the dust off the doorframe with a rag.

examples.ko: 문틀 위에 작은 화분을 올려 두었어요.
examples.en: I put a small flowerpot on top of the doorframe.

examples.ko: 이 문틀은 나무가 아니라 철로 만들었어요.
examples.en: This doorframe is made of metal, not wood.

explain: 문짝을 끼우는 둘레의 틀이에요. 창문 쪽은 '창틀'이라고 하고, 바닥 쪽의 턱은 '문턱'이라고 해서 서로 달라요.

phrases.en: I was rushing out and bumped my shoulder on the doorframe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문틀은 사람이 지나가다가 부딪히기 쉬운 곳이라 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: People often bump into doorframes when passing through, so this is a common pairing.

phrases.en: He leaned against the doorframe and waited for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문 옆에 기대어 서 있는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone leaning in a doorway.

phrases.en: I replaced the old doorframe with a new one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 수리하는 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears when talking about home repairs.

explain_en: It is the frame around the opening that holds the door. For windows it is '창틀', and the raised bar at the bottom is '문턱', which is a different thing.

examples.en: I sprayed water on the plant with a spray bottle.
Please fill the spray bottle with water.

examples.ko: 분무기가 고장 나서 물이 나오지 않아요.
examples.en: The sprayer is broken and no water comes out.

examples.ko: 머리가 뻗쳐서 분무기로 물을 살짝 뿌렸어요.
examples.en: My hair was sticking up, so I lightly misted it with water.
Using a spray bottle is handy when ironing.
I bought a new sprayer and left it on the balcony.

explain: 물이나 액체를 안개처럼 가늘게 뿜어 주는 도구예요. 화분에 물을 주는 '물뿌리개'는 물줄기가 나오는 점이 달라요. 일상에서는 '스프레이'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I watered the plant with a spray bottle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '분무기' 대신 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common everyday word used instead of 분무기.

phrases.en: I sprayed water on the laundry and ironed it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구를 말할 때 '-로'를 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 로 to say which tool you use.

phrases.example: 분무기에 물을 담아서 화분 옆에 두었어요.
phrases.en: I filled the sprayer with water and put it next to the pot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사용하기 전에 물을 넣는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The action of putting water in before use.
phrases.en_equiv: to fill a sprayer with water

explain_en: It is a tool that sprays water or liquid in a fine mist. A '물뿌리개' (watering can), used for watering plants, differs in that it pours out streams of water. In daily talk people also often say '스프레이'.

examples.en: I put the meat on the grill and cook it.

examples.ko: 생선을 구울 때는 석쇠에 기름을 바르세요.
examples.en: When grilling fish, put oil on the grill.
The grill was too old, so I bought a new one.

examples.ko: 석쇠 자국이 선명한 구이가 맛있어 보여요.
examples.en: The grilled food with clear grill marks looks delicious.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 숯불 위 석쇠에서 오징어를 구우셨어요.
examples.en: Grandpa grilled squid on a grill over charcoal.

examples.ko: 캠핑 갈 때 석쇠를 꼭 챙겨 가요.
examples.en: I always bring a grill when I go camping.

explain: 불 위에 올려 음식을 직접 굽는 철망이에요. 석쇠에 구운 요리는 '석쇠구이'라고도 하고, 평평한 '불판'과는 모양이 달라요.

phrases.en: Tonight's dinner is grilled fish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 석쇠에 구운 요리를 가리키는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name for a dish cooked on a grill.

phrases.en: Meat tastes better when grilled on a grate.
phrases.nuance_ko: '굽다'와 함께 쓰는 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic use together with 굽다.

phrases.example: 고기를 먹은 뒤에 석쇠를 깨끗이 씻어요.
phrases.en: After eating meat, I wash the grill well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사용한 뒤에 정리할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when cleaning up after cooking.

explain_en: It is a wire grate placed over a fire to cook food directly. Food cooked on it is also called '석쇠구이', and it differs in shape from a flat '불판' (grill plate).

examples.en: The speedometer says we are already doing 100 kilometers per hour.
The speedometer broke, so I took it in for repair.
Check the speedometer often when you drive.
I attached a speedometer to my new bicycle.
The speedometer needle keeps shaking.

examples.ko: 속도계에 숫자가 크게 나와서 보기 편해요.
examples.en: The numbers show big on the speedometer, so it is easy to read.

explain: 자동차에서는 속도계가 '계기판' 안에 들어 있어서 '계기판을 봐요'라고도 말해요. 자전거나 운동 기구에 다는 작은 속도계도 같은 말로 불러요.

phrases.en: The speedometer needle is rising fast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바늘로 속도를 보여 주는 속도계를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a speedometer that shows speed with a needle.

phrases.en: I checked the speed on the dashboard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자동차에서는 속도계가 있는 판 전체를 '계기판'이라고 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: In a car, the whole panel that includes the speedometer is called 계기판.

phrases.en: I attached a speedometer to my bicycle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기구에 새로 붙일 때 '달다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '달다' when attaching one to equipment.

explain_en: In a car the speedometer sits inside the '계기판' (instrument panel), so people also say '계기판을 봐요'. Small speedometers for bicycles or exercise machines are called by the same word.

examples.ko: 고장 난 문을 아버지가 손봐 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father fixed up the broken door for me.

examples.ko: 이사 가기 전에 낡은 집을 조금 손볼 거예요.
examples.en: I will fix up the old house a bit before moving.

examples.ko: 발표 자료를 한 번 더 손보고 제출하세요.
examples.en: Touch up the presentation material once more before you submit it.

examples.ko: 수도꼭지가 샌다고 해서 사람을 불러 손봤어요.
examples.en: The faucet was leaking, so I called someone to fix it.

examples.ko: 글을 조금만 손보면 훨씬 자연스러울 거예요.
examples.en: If you touch up the writing a little, it will be much more natural.

examples.ko: 자전거를 손본 뒤에 같이 타러 가요.
examples.en: Let's go riding together after I fix up the bike.

explain: '고치다'보다 가볍게, 전부 바꾸지 않고 필요한 곳만 만져서 좋게 한다는 느낌이에요. 집, 기계, 글, 계획에 두루 써요. 사람에게 '손 좀 봐 주겠다'고 하면 혼내 주겠다는 위협이라서 조심해야 해요.

phrases.example: 말을 안 들으면 손 좀 봐 줄 거예요.
phrases.en: to teach someone a lesson
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람에게 쓰면 혼내 주거나 벌을 주겠다는 위협적인 말이에요. 친한 사이의 농담으로도 쓰지만 조심해야 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said about a person, it is a threat to scold or punish. It can be a joke between friends, but use it carefully.

explain_en: Compared with 고치다, 손보다 feels lighter: you touch only the parts that need work instead of changing everything. It works for houses, machines, writing, and plans. Saying '손 좀 봐 주겠다' to a person is a threat meaning you will teach them a lesson, so be careful.

dis.h: informal: tidy up, fix up lightly

p.n: 손보다 sounds like a light fix-up; 고치다 can mean a bigger repair.

examples.en: This speaker is stereo, so the sound feels three-dimensional.
The song sounds rich when I listen in stereo.
I watched a movie with stereo earphones.
In the old days, every living room had a big stereo.

examples.ko: 왼쪽과 오른쪽 소리가 다른 게 스테레오예요.
examples.en: When the left and right sounds differ, that is stereo.
It is a stereo recording, so you can feel where each instrument is.

explain: 한쪽에서만 소리가 나는 '모노'의 반대로, 왼쪽과 오른쪽이 다르게 나오는 소리를 말해요. 오디오 기계 자체를 '스테레오'라고 부르기도 하지만 요즘은 '스피커', '오디오'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 스테레오 스피커로 음악을 들으니 소리가 좋아요.
phrases.en: The sound is good when I listen to music on stereo speakers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 왼쪽과 오른쪽 소리가 따로 나오는 스피커를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Speakers that play separate left and right sound.

phrases.example: 이 영화는 스테레오 소리가 아주 좋아요.
phrases.en: This movie has really good stereo sound.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리의 종류를 말할 때 '소리' 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before 'sound' to name the type of sound.

phrases.example: 이 노래는 스테레오로 들으면 더 풍성해요.
phrases.en: This song sounds richer when you listen to it in stereo.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로'를 붙여 어떤 방식으로 듣는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '으로', it says in what way you listen.

explain_en: It is the opposite of '모노', where one channel carries all the sound; in stereo the left and right sides differ. Some people call the audio machine itself a '스테레오', but today '스피커' and '오디오' are more common.

examples.en: I swept the dust into the dustpan.
The broom and dustpan are next to the entrance.
The dustpan broke, so I bought a new one.
The child held the dustpan for me.
I carefully cleaned up the glass pieces with a dustpan.
Could you bring me the dustpan?

explain: 보통 '빗자루'와 한 쌍으로 기억하면 좋아요. 쓸어 모은 먼지나 쓰레기를 받아서 담는 도구예요. 발음은 [쓰레받끼]예요.

phrases.en: I'll hold the dustpan for you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓸어 모은 먼지를 받을 수 있게 바닥에 대 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for holding the dustpan down to catch swept dust.

phrases.en: I swept the glass pieces into the dustpan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓰레기를 쓸어서 담는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes sweeping trash into the dustpan.

phrases.en: I emptied the dustpan into the trash can.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청소를 마치고 담긴 것을 버릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when tossing out the contents after cleaning.

explain_en: It is easiest to remember as a pair with '빗자루' (broom). It is the tool that catches the swept dust or trash. It is pronounced [쓰레받끼].

examples.ko: 컵을 엎지르면 바로 닦아야 얼룩이 안 생겨요.
examples.en: If you spill a cup, wipe it up right away so it doesn't stain.

examples.ko: 책상 위에 커피를 엎지르고 놀라서 소리를 질렀어요.
examples.en: I spilled coffee on the desk and cried out in surprise.

examples.ko: 엎지르지 않게 컵을 두 손으로 잡으세요.
examples.en: Hold the cup with both hands so you don't spill it.
I spilled the soup, so I had to change my clothes.

examples.ko: 엎지른 물을 닦다 보니 시간이 다 갔어요.
examples.en: Wiping up the spilled water took all my time.
You could spill it if you're careless, so be careful.

explain: '르' 불규칙이라서 '엎질러요, 엎질렀어요'로 활용해요. '쏟다'는 일부러 부을 때도 쓰지만 '엎지르다'는 보통 실수로 그릇이 기울어 흘릴 때 써요. 사람이 주어이고, 물건이 저절로 쏟아지면 '엎질러지다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I was walking in a hurry and spilled my juice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '르' 불규칙 활용이라서 '엎지르어요'가 아니라 '엎질렀어요'라고 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is an irregular '르' conjugation, so you say 엎질렀어요, not 엎지르어요.

phrases.en: Please don't spill the hot soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조심하라고 부탁하거나 주의를 줄 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask someone to be careful or to warn them.

phrases.en: The child spilled water, so the floor got wet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '물, 커피, 우유'처럼 흘러내리는 것과 함께 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing with liquids such as water, coffee, or milk.

explain_en: It is a '르' irregular verb, so it conjugates as '엎질러요' and '엎질렀어요'. '쏟다' can be used for pouring on purpose, but '엎지르다' is normally for tipping a container by mistake. A person is the subject; when something spills by itself, use '엎질러지다'.

examples.en: I brought a new display cabinet into the living room.

examples.ko: 장식장 안에 여행에서 사 온 기념품이 있어요.
examples.en: There are souvenirs from my trips inside the display cabinet.
Grandma's display cabinet is full of ceramics.
This display cabinet has glass doors.

examples.ko: 장식장이 너무 커서 거실이 좁아 보여요.
examples.en: The display cabinet is so big that the living room looks small.
I'm using it as a display cabinet instead of a bookcase.

explain: 물건을 넣어 두는 가구가 아니라 보여 주려고 두는 물건을 진열하는 장이에요. 책을 꽂는 '책장', 옷이나 물건을 넣는 '서랍장'과 구분해서 불러요.

phrases.en: I displayed my collected models in the display cabinet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 보이도록 놓을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when putting things out for show.

phrases.en: The glass display cabinet is full of pretty cups.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안이 보이는 장식장을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for cabinets you can see into.

phrases.en: I put a family photo on top of the display cabinet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가구 위에 물건을 놓을 때 조사와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with particles when placing things on furniture.
phrases.en_equiv: on top of the display cabinet

explain_en: It is a cabinet for showing off items rather than just storing them. It is distinguished from a '책장' (bookcase) and a '서랍장' (chest of drawers).

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 전기면도기를 꼭 챙겨요.
examples.en: I always pack my electric razor when I travel.

examples.ko: 전기면도기는 물 없이도 쓸 수 있어서 편해요.
examples.en: An electric razor is convenient because you can use it without water.
I gave my father an electric razor as a birthday present.

examples.ko: 충전해서 쓰는 전기면도기라서 선이 필요 없어요.
examples.en: It's a rechargeable electric razor, so no cord is needed.
My electric razor broke, so I bought a new one.

examples.ko: 전기면도기 날을 갈아야 할 때가 됐어요.
examples.en: It's time to replace the blades of the electric razor.

explain: 그냥 '면도기'라고 하면 손으로 쓰는 날 면도기를 떠올리는 사람이 많아서, 전기로 움직이는 것은 '전기'를 붙여 구별해요. 대화에서는 '면도기'만 말해도 상황으로 알 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I bought a new razor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서는 '전기' 없이도 쓰지만 날 면도기를 뜻할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used without 전기 in conversation, but it can mean a blade razor.

phrases.en: I shave with an electric razor every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 도구를 쓰는지 말할 때 '-로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use -로 to say which tool you use.
phrases.en_equiv: to shave with an electric razor

phrases.en: I charged my electric razor before the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배터리를 채울 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for charging the battery.

explain_en: Plain '면도기' often brings to mind a manual blade razor, so the electric kind is distinguished by adding '전기'. In conversation, just saying '면도기' is often fine because the situation makes it clear.

examples.ko: 컵은 찬장 두 번째 칸에 있어요.
examples.en: The cups are on the second shelf of the cupboard.
The cupboard door doesn't close well.
I put the new dishes away in the cupboard.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 찬장에서 과자를 몰래 꺼내 먹었어요.
examples.en: As a child I secretly took snacks out of the cupboard.

examples.ko: 큰 접시는 찬장 위에 올려 놓아요.
examples.en: I put the big plates on top of the cupboard.

examples.ko: 찬장이 좁아서 그릇을 더 못 넣어요.
examples.en: The cupboard is small, so I can't fit more dishes.

explain: 부엌에서 그릇이나 음식을 넣어 두는 장이에요. 요즘 새 집에서는 '수납장'이라고 하는 경우가 많고, '찬장'은 조금 옛날 느낌도 있어요.

phrases.en: Please put the bowls in the cupboard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그릇이나 음식을 보관할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for storing dishes or food.

phrases.en: I took a plate out of the cupboard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찬장 안의 물건을 쓸 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for taking things out of the cupboard to use.
phrases.en_equiv: to take out of the cupboard

phrases.en: The new house has a lot of storage cabinets.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요즘 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요. 부엌뿐 아니라 여러 물건을 넣는 장에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word used more often these days, for cabinets holding many kinds of things, not just in the kitchen.

explain_en: It is a cabinet in the kitchen for keeping dishes and food. In newer homes people often say '수납장' (storage cabinet), and '찬장' can sound a little old-fashioned.

examples.en: I took a sleeping bag when I went camping.
It was warm once I got inside the sleeping bag.
A winter sleeping bag is thicker than a summer one.
I borrowed a sleeping bag from my friend.
The children rolled out sleeping bags in the living room and slept.

examples.ko: 침낭은 접어서 작은 가방에 넣을 수 있어요.
examples.en: A sleeping bag can be folded into a small bag.

explain: '침낭'은 캠핑이나 등산에서 바닥에 펴고 그 안에 들어가 자는 주머니 모양의 잠자리예요. '침낭을 펴다/말다', '침낭에 들어가다'로 써요. 이불은 덮는 것이고 침낭은 몸 전체를 감싸요.

phrases.en: I spread out the sleeping bag inside the tent and lay down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘 준비를 할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation used when getting ready to sleep.

phrases.en: In the mountains, you have to sleep in a sleeping bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '-에서'를 붙여 자는 장소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The particle -에서 marks where you sleep.
phrases.en_equiv: to sleep in a sleeping bag

phrases.example: 아침에 일어나서 침낭을 말아 가방에 넣었어요.
phrases.en: In the morning I got up, rolled up the sleeping bag, and put it in my bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사용한 뒤 정리할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요. 반대는 '침낭을 펴다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when packing up after use. The opposite is 침낭을 펴다.
phrases.en_equiv: to roll up a sleeping bag

explain_en: '침낭' is a pouch-shaped sleeping bag you lay on the ground and climb into, used for camping and hiking. You say '침낭을 펴다/말다' and '침낭에 들어가다'. A blanket is something you cover with, while a sleeping bag wraps your whole body.

examples.ko: 톱날이 무뎌서 나무가 잘 안 잘려요.
examples.en: The saw blade is dull, so the wood doesn't cut well.
Be careful not to cut your hand on the saw blade.
I bought a new saw blade at the hardware store.
My father sharpened the saw blade and used it again.
The saw blade spun fast, and it was scary.

examples.ko: 이 칼은 톱날 모양이라 빵이 잘 썰려요.
examples.en: This knife has a serrated edge, so it cuts bread well.

explain: 톱에서 이가 나 있는 날 부분을 말해요. '칼날', '가위날'처럼 도구의 날카로운 부분은 '-날'로 말해요. 빵칼처럼 톱니 모양의 날은 '톱날 모양'이라고 설명하기도 해요.

phrases.en: The saw blade is sharp, so be careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날의 상태를 설명하는 형용사와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with an adjective describing the blade's condition.

phrases.en: My father sharpened the saw blade on a whetstone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무뎌진 날을 다시 날카롭게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when making a dull blade sharp again.

phrases.en: This bread knife has a serrated shape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이가 난 모양을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a toothed shape.

explain_en: This is the toothed cutting part of a saw. For tools, the sharp part is named with '-날', as in '칼날' (knife blade) and '가위날' (scissor blade). A bread knife's serrated edge can be described as '톱날 모양'.

en: single large pane of glass; full glass wall

examples.ko: 이 카페는 통유리라서 밖이 잘 보여요.
examples.en: This café has full glass walls, so you can see outside well.

examples.ko: 거실에 통유리 창이 있어서 햇빛이 많이 들어와요.
examples.en: The living room has a big glass window, so a lot of sunlight comes in.

examples.ko: 통유리 너머로 눈 오는 풍경을 구경했어요.
examples.en: I watched the snowy scenery through the big glass window.

examples.ko: 통유리는 겨울에 좀 추울 수 있어요.
examples.en: Full glass walls can be a bit cold in winter.

examples.ko: 새 건물은 앞면이 전부 통유리로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: The new building's front is entirely made of large single sheets of glass.

examples.ko: 통유리에 새가 부딪히지 않게 스티커를 붙였어요.
examples.en: I put stickers on the big glass window so birds won't hit it.

explain: 창틀로 나누지 않고 한 장으로 크게 만든 유리를 말해요. 카페나 새 건물, 거실 창에서 많이 쓰는 말이에요. 안이 밝고 전망이 좋다는 좋은 느낌으로 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: The front of the building is made of one big glass pane.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇이 통유리로 만들어졌는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what is made of a single large glass pane.
phrases.en_equiv: is made of a full glass wall

phrases.en: I can see the sea beyond the full glass wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벽 전체가 유리일 때 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the whole wall is glass.

phrases.en: Thanks to the big glass window, the house is very bright.
phrases.nuance_ko: 통유리의 좋은 점을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to mention the good side of a large glass pane.

explain_en: It refers to one large sheet of glass that isn't divided by a frame. The word is common for cafés, new buildings and living room windows. People often use it with a positive feel of brightness and a good view.

examples.ko: 여름에는 해수욕장마다 파라솔과 튜브를 빌려주는 가게가 생겨요.
examples.en: In summer, shops that rent out parasols and tubes appear at every beach.

examples.ko: 햇빛이 너무 강하니까 파라솔 아래에 앉아요.
examples.en: The sun is too strong, so let's sit under the parasol.

examples.ko: 카페 밖에 파라솔이 있어서 앉기 편해요.
examples.en: There are parasols outside the cafe, so it's comfortable to sit.
The wind blew and the parasol almost flew away.
I put up the parasol and read a book in the shade.

examples.ko: 파라솔 하나에 의자가 네 개 있어요.
examples.en: There are four chairs for each parasol.

explain: 손에 드는 양산이 아니라 바닷가나 카페 야외 자리에 세워 두는 큰 우산을 말할 때 주로 써요. 손에 드는 것은 '양산'이라고 해요. 보통 '파라솔을 펴다/접다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: As soon as we arrived at the beach, we opened the parasol.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우산처럼 펼치는 동작을 말해요. 자리를 잡을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes opening it up like an umbrella. Often said when setting up a spot.

phrases.example: 해가 지자 파라솔을 접고 집에 갔어요.
phrases.en: When the sun set, we folded the parasol and went home.
phrases.nuance_ko: '펴다'의 반대 동작이에요. 돌아갈 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite action of '펴다'. Used when leaving.

phrases.example: 우리는 파라솔 아래에서 시원한 음료를 마셨어요.
phrases.en: We drank cold drinks under the parasol.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그늘 아래에서 쉰다는 말이에요. 장소를 말할 때 조사와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means resting in the shade. Used with a particle to name a place.

explain_en: It usually means a large umbrella set up at a beach or an outdoor cafe, not one you carry. The handheld sun umbrella is called '양산'. You say '파라솔을 펴다/접다' (open/close).

examples.ko: 할머니는 베란다 흔들의자에 앉아 책을 읽어요.
examples.en: Grandma sits in the rocking chair on the balcony and reads.
Grandma put the baby to sleep in the rocking chair.
I want to put a rocking chair in the living room.
This rocking chair rocks slowly back and forth.
I can hear the rocking chair creaking in the room.
My father takes a nap in the rocking chair.

explain: 사전에 한 단어로 실려 있어서 '흔들 의자'가 아니라 붙여 써요. 베란다나 거실에 두고 편하게 쉬는 의자라서 여유, 휴식과 함께 이야기할 때가 많아요.

phrases.en: I feel relaxed when I sit in a rocking chair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의자에 앉는 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to use the word.
phrases.en_equiv: to sit in a rocking chair

phrases.en: On weekends I take a nap in the rocking chair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편하게 쉬거나 낮잠을 자는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when picturing someone resting or napping comfortably.
phrases.en_equiv: to rest in a rocking chair

phrases.en: I bought a rocking chair to put in the living room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 사거나 놓는 이야기에서 '사다·놓다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '사다' or '놓다' when talking about buying or placing it.

explain_en: It is listed in the dictionary as one word, so you write it without a space. People picture it on a balcony or in a living room for relaxing, so it often comes up when talking about rest and leisure.
